items.bewering: Die eerste boere (in 'Nie elke plek het alles nie', 'Ruil sonder geld' en 'Deel en saamwerk')
items.blok: Nie elke plek het alles nie
items.bron: South African History Online, 'The first farmers' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/archive/african-farmers-southern-africa) and 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/article/pre-colonial-history-southern-africa): the Bantu-speaking farmers who grew sorghum and millet and kept cattle, sheep and goats are the established 'first farmers' of southern Africa, and both San and Khoekhoe were already there when they arrived. The lesson uses the term as a name and sets it beside the San and Khoikhoi, which matches that usage. Note for a person, not a fault: Khoekhoe herders kept sheep and later cattle before or around the same time, so 'eerste' holds for crop-growing farmers rather than for everyone who kept animals. The lesson makes no claim that would lead a learner past that point.

items.bewering: Die eerste boere het nie almal op een plek gewoon nie.
items.blok: Nie elke plek het alles nie
items.bron: SAHO, 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/article/pre-colonial-history-southern-africa) and 'The first farmers' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/archive/african-farmers-southern-africa): farming communities settled across many parts of the region, traced by different pottery styles.

items.bewering: Op party plekke het daar yster of koper in die klippe gesit.
items.blok: Nie elke plek het alles nie
items.bron: A. Moffett (UCT), 'Iron Age mining links ancient SA to the world', Mail & Guardian, 15 Aug 2014 (https://mg.co.za/2014-08-15-iron-age-mining-links-ancient-sa-to-the-world/): iron and copper were mined and worked at Phalaborwa and other sources; SAHO pre-colonial history: early farmers made iron tools and copper ornaments. Ore deposits are local, not everywhere.

items.bewering: Ander plekke het soutpanne of goeie weiveld vir die beeste gehad.
items.blok: Nie elke plek het alles nie
items.bron: A. Antonites, 'The Salt of Baleni' (MA, University of Pretoria, 2005; https://repository.up.ac.za/items/c69a1fb0-e914-4cf9-82f9-6153f28fb205/full): salt made by Early Iron Age farming communities at a salt source in Limpopo; Tswaing crater ('place of salt'), a salt lake harvested by Sotho-Tswana communities (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tswaing_crater); SAHO 'The first farmers': cattle were central to farming life and needed grazing.

items.bewering: Dinge wat mense gebruik, soos yster, sout en weiveld, noem ons hulpbronne.
items.blok: Nie elke plek het alles nie
items.bron: UNISA GEOTERM glossary, 'resources' (https://gama.unisa.ac.za/geoterm/concepts/232/en): things of natural origin needed by and of value to people. Iron, salt and grazing all fit.

items.bewering: Nie elke plek het dieselfde hulpbronne gehad nie. Daarom het mense van een plek goedere met mense van 'n ander plek geruil.
items.blok: Nie elke plek het alles nie
items.bron: Antonites 2005 (UP repository), citing Plug and Pistorius 1999: Lowveld iron producers such as Phalaborwa traded iron for food to make up for an arid climate; a Baleni study notes that a salt-making village obtained food by trading salt. Moffett, Mail & Guardian 2014: salt, produce, cattle, iron and copper moved along regional trade routes. Uneven resources as a reason for exchange is well supported.

items.bewering: Die boere het nie met munte of papiergeld betaal nie.
items.bron: SAHO 'The first farmers' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/archive/african-farmers-southern-africa): cattle were the main source of wealth and the medium of exchange; no coinage is described. Moffett, Mail & Guardian 2014: iron hoes and copper rods (marale) served for bride-price, tribute and fines. So there was no coin or paper money, which is what the sentence says. Things like cattle and hoes stood in for money in some exchanges, and the sentence does not deny that.

items.bewering: Hulle het een ding direk vir iets anders geruil, en dit noem ons ruilhandel.
items.bron: Standard definition of barter (Dutch/Afrikaans ruilhandel): goods or services exchanged directly for other goods or services without money (interglot.nl 'bartering' -> ruilhandel; marxists.org Dutch economic dictionary, 'ruil'). SAHO and Moffett as above for exchange among the farmers.

items.bewering: 'n Gesin met ekstra sout kon dit vir 'n skoffel van yster ruil.
items.bron: This is a made-up example with 'kon'. Both items are documented as exchange goods in the same networks: salt (Antonites 2005; Moffett 2014) and iron hoes (Moffett 2014: iron hoes widely traded and used in payments). I found no source naming this exact salt-for-hoe swap, and the sentence does not claim one. The example is plausible and does not mislead.

items.bewering: So het albei kante iets gekry wat hulle nodig gehad het.
items.bron: Follows from the barter definition and from Plug and Pistorius as cited in Antonites 2005: exchange met needs on both sides, e.g. iron for food.

items.bewering: Sout om kos te geur.
items.bron: Salt as a trade good: Moffett, Mail & Guardian 2014; Antonites 2005 (salt produced for a consumer population, part of Lowveld trade). Flavouring food is a real use (salt was also used to preserve food; the item does not say flavouring was the only use).

items.bewering: Beeste, wat baie werd was.
items.bron: SAHO 'The first farmers': cattle were the main source of wealth and the medium of exchange, used for bride wealth and fines. Moffett 2014: cattle among the goods moving along trade routes.

items.bewering: Yster en ystergereedskap soos skoffels en byle.
items.bron: Moffett 2014: iron hoes widely traded and used in payments; SAHO 'The first farmers': iron tools, especially hoes, were very important, and hunter-gatherers got iron tools from farmers in exchange for labour, beads and skins. Iron axes are among the iron tools the farmers made.

items.bewering: Koper om armbande en ander mooi dinge van te maak.
items.bron: Moffett 2014: metal goods 'from iron hoes to copper bangles' widely consumed across southern Africa; copper traded as wire and rods. SAHO pre-colonial history: farmers made copper ornaments.

items.bewering: Graan en kleipotte.
items.bron: Moffett 2014: agricultural produce among traded goods; SAHO 'The first farmers': hunter-gatherers got food from farmers in exchange for labour and goods. Early Iron Age pottery found at hunter-gatherer sites such as Likoaeng, Lesotho, shows ongoing contact and exchange with farming communities (Nature Human Behaviour 2020, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-020-0859-0, and the work it cites).

items.bewering: Die eerste boere het saam met die San en die Khoikhoi in Suider-Afrika gewoon.
items.bron: SAHO 'Pre-colonial history of southern Africa': both San and Khoekhoe were in southern Africa when the first Bantu-speaking farmers arrived; SAHO 'The first farmers': San and Khoikhoi objects on farming sites suggest they lived alongside each other, and some intermarried.

items.bewering: Die drie groepe het goedere, kennis en vaardighede met mekaar gedeel.
items.bron: SAHO 'The first farmers': farmers traded with and employed hunter-gatherers; words and click sounds from San and Khoi languages entered Bantu languages. M. Hirst, Amathole Museum, Imvubu 21:1 (2009) (https://www.amatholemuseum.co.za/the-khoisan-of-the-eastern-cape/): Xhosa got ostrich-eggshell beads by barter; Xhosa healers took over a Khoisan healing dance; shared techniques and rituals.

items.bewering: Maar elke groep het grond en water op sy eie manier gebruik. Dit kon soms tot mededinging en spanning tussen die groepe lei.
items.bron: Ways of using land differed: hunting and gathering, herding, and mixed farming with crops (SAHO pre-colonial history). Conflict: SAHO 'The first farmers', Eastern Cape rock paintings show 'a clash between two ways of life'; Amathole Museum, Imvubu 2009: Khoisan-Xhosa contact marked by trade, intermarriage and warfare. The hedged 'kon soms' fits the evidence.

items.bewering: Tog het ruil en saamwerk die groepe met mekaar verbind.
items.bron: SAHO 'The first farmers': trade, labour and intermarriage between farmers and San/Khoikhoi; Amathole Museum, Imvubu 2009: the amaGqunukhwebe were a chiefdom of mixed Khoi-Xhosa descent.

items.bewering: ruilhandel: Wanneer mense goedere of dienste direk vir mekaar ruil, sonder geld.
items.bron: Standard definition of barter: goods or services exchanged directly without money (interglot.nl, barter -> ruilhandel; Dutch economic dictionary on marxists.org, 'ruil').

items.bewering: hulpbron: Iets wat mense gebruik om in hulle behoeftes te voorsien.
items.bron: UNISA GEOTERM 'resources' (https://gama.unisa.ac.za/geoterm/concepts/232/en): things needed by and of value to people; Zimmermann's classic definition of a resource as something that meets a human want (quoted in INFLIBNET resource geography course, https://ebooks.inflibnet.ac.in/geop03/chapter/scope-and-relevance-of-resource-geography/).

items.bewering: soutpan: 'n Vlak plek waar water opdroog en 'n laag sout agterlaat.
items.bron: Salt pan (geology), Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_pan_(geology)): a flat area where water that cannot drain away evaporates and leaves salt and minerals behind; American Heritage definition: a shallow basin where water collects, evaporates and leaves salt. 'Vlak' (flat or shallow) is right either way.

items.bewering: weiveld: Oop veld met gras of bossies waar vee kan wei.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English, 'veld' (https://dsae.co.za/entry/veld/e07599): natural uncultivated vegetation used as pasture; 'mixed veld' (https://dsae.co.za/entry/mixed-veld/e04780): grass and scrub; NWGA Wolboer weidingsgids 2013 uses 'natuurlike weiveld' for grazing veld.

items.bewering: mededinging: Wanneer groepe probeer om dieselfde ding vir hulleself te kry.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'mededinging' (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/mededinging): competition, rivalry for the same thing (synonyms concurrentie, wedstrijd). The definition is narrowed to groups, which fits how the lesson uses the word, and is not false.

opsomming: All 24 checkable claims, including the five definitions and five list items, are supported by archive, museum and academic sources, the lesson has no analogies, and its one superlative ('die eerste boere') is used correctly as the topic's name; the salt-for-hoe swap is a made-up example built from two documented trade goods and needs no change.
